item.title: Nobel laureate leads University of Hong Kong study to spot diseases early
item.description: The University of Hong Kong (HKU) has launched a 20-year study tracking blood samples from 15,000 locals to build an affordable screening tool that spots cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular diseases and chronic respiratory illnesses before symptoms appear. The “Protecting.Health Hong Kong” study, launched by HKU’s Institute for Precision Prevention on Tuesday, is led by its director Professor Ferenc Krausz, a 2023 Nobel laureate in physics who was recently recruited by the university. item.title: Chinese Texans hope Democratic wins will overturn Senate Bill 17 property restrictions
item.description: At a cafe in Austin, Texas, a group gathers on a sunny Friday morning. Just a few years ago, many were strangers. Today, one has brought biscuits, another T-shirts emblazoned with “Asian Texans Vote”. They have bonded through their shared opposition to Texas Senate Bill 17 (SB17), which became law last year. “If you have to say one positive thing about all this … it’s that I made friends with a group of people I never knew before,” says Hugh Li, president of the Austin Chinese-American Network...
